bluf: Semetis is an Omnicom owned performance media and analytics agency in Brussels, with 39 named team members on its site, selling digital advertising across search, social, display, programmatic and video alongside business intelligence and training to enterprise advertisers. Its one dated move is two wins at the 20th AMMA Awards in 2025-06, and its newest direction is GEO guidance with no GEO service line behind it. A rival should know the Horus read makes it most exposed to KJ6 at net -0.855, driven by the paid search and paid social hours it leads with, and that 7 of its 9 clients are names only.
doing:
The positioning line, an Omnicom owned Brussels agency combining integrated digital advertising across search, social, display, programmatic and video with business intelligence, analytics and training, decodes as a holdco media buyer that also builds the measurement behind the buying and teaches client teams to use it. The headline claim, Digital Agency of the Year at Belgium's 2023 IAB MIXX Awards, is quoted as a claim, as is its own release saying WARC placed it first among digital and specialist agencies for effectiveness in 2023.

The sold mix leads with two lines scored 3. Data & Measurement: the title pairs advertising with Business Intelligence, and the services list web analytics, tag management, dashboarding and data interpretation. Paid Search: the title headlines Digital Advertising and the meta leads with search engine marketing. Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV score 2 as core lines, the first on an offer spanning social, mobile and video, the second on display, programmatic and video plus an AMMA Best Media Strategy nomination. Five lines score 1, among them AI Search / GEO, retail media and SEO, for a breadth of 9. The record lists no proprietary product and no partners, only services such as trainings, custom solutions and technology built in house or by third parties.

The AI posture is commentary, not a product: it publishes GEO and AI search guidance, with GEO articles dated Dec 2025, and cites AI powered audience targeting in its Atol case, while AI Automation / Agents scores 0 and no AI service line shows. The one dated move is two AMMA wins in 2025-06. It lists two openings, a Digital Business Analyst listing tagged Business Intern and an office manager page. The record holds no pricing signal. Conspicuously absent for a measurement seller: any ad pixel on its own site, any proprietary measurement product, and any dated case study.
clients:
The ICP is enterprise, and the record lists six verticals: retail (DIY, garden, electronics, optical), telecommunications, insurance, home security, rail infrastructure and the public sector, and consumer health. The home market is Belgium, served from a single Brussels office.

The needs read holds 9 named clients, 2 observed and 7 names only, drawn from 6 client logos, 2 case studies and 1 award entry. Atol is observed through a case study slug, driving campaign success with AI powered audiences, which the read codes AI and automation plus local and lead generation. Vanden Borre is observed through a slug on driving demand for Vanden Borre life with a blue ocean digital media strategy, coded local and lead generation. Both slugs describe media and audience work, so paid performance is likely the truer need and the lead generation code likely overstates local demand (moderate confidence); neither case carries a date in the record. Verisure, Orange, Infrabel, Brico, AXA and Jardiland are logos with no described work, and UPSA Digest Forte is an award entry, the homepage AMMA Best Media Strategy nomination with the edition not shown; for these seven the need is inferred from the sold mix, paid search and measurement first.

Orange also sits on the books of artefact and bluerank, the one shared client.

What the base needs next: under KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better) these enterprise advertisers likely keep buying analytics and dashboards, a tailwind for its lead line, while under KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) the paid execution hours are likely the part they automate first (moderate confidence).
house: Say and do: 0 of 2 tested lines practised. Paid Social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: the LinkedIn Ad Library name query returns 0 ads, so it sells social and B2B demand without buying any itself. Paid Search is unknown because the Transparency Center lookup was blocked, so the record holds no Google ad count or sample line. The Radar lists both contradictions as gaps. The stack shows gtm only, with no CMS detected, no pixels, no test tools and no ABM stack, thin for a firm selling tag management and web analytics. Content velocity cannot be read: the deepen pass found no readable sitemap URLs, so the sitemap, 90 day and 365 day counts all read 0, and 0 AI topic URLs register. It publishes no llms.txt and blocks no AI crawlers.
market:
The Horus read scores Semetis -4.5 on the tailwind index, Neutral band, percentile 13. It is best placed for KJ1 and KJ9 (net 0.292 each); worse measurement is a tailwind for its Data & Measurement line. Its exposure is heavy: KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out (net -0.855, driven by Paid Search and Paid Social), and KJ5, the price of attention splits in two (net -0.18). Best fit is The Walled Oasis at 53/100. It is making P4, supplying the inputs automation runs on, partial on P1 and P7, absent on P2, P6 and P8.

The Monsoon read is 48.7, band Breeze, with migration 56.2 above displacement 41.2: the work could move, but enterprise buyers are less price led. The verdict puts 46 in the sold mix, Paid Search (12) and Data & Measurement (9) leading, sends the work 45% to Africa and the Maghreb, 30% to South and Southeast Asia and 20% to Eastern Europe, and finds automation overlapping 37% of movable hours. The footprint is inferred; its one onshore phrase is a service name.
openings:
The strongest opening is the execution layer. KJ6 is its largest exposure at net -0.855, driven by the paid search and paid social hours it leads with; the Monsoon read finds automation overlapping 37% of movable hours; and P8 is absent, with no sign of testing ads inside AI assistants. A rival offering automated, outcome priced paid media with measurement attached is likely, moderate confidence, to pry execution budgets loose from its retail and telecom accounts, leaving Semetis the BI work that KJ9 favors. Falsifier: a dated Semetis case or release showing assistant ad tests or outcome pricing for a named account.

The say and do contradictions make the opener: it sells paid social and LinkedIn demand without a social pixel or a single LinkedIn ad of its own. It writes GEO guidance but sells no GEO line, so an audited AI visibility offer meets no incumbent product.

Orange, also on the artefact and bluerank books, is the shopper to call first. Seven of its 9 clients are names only, so what it does for Verisure, AXA or Infrabel is a question for those clients, not a known quantity.
watch: Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would reach an Omnicom owned specialist directly and sharpen KJ6, its largest exposure.

Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: growth below 10% would flag cannibalization of the search engine marketing it leads with, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live would confirm S1 and put its absent P8 move under pressure.

Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users versus search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth would confirm the UGC starvation risk under KJ1, the tailwind its GEO guidance addresses.
Follow up the 2025-06 AMMA wins and the homepage UPSA Digest Forte nomination, edition not shown: a dated case with described work would turn an award entry into an observed engagement.
Follow up its two listed openings, the Digital Business Analyst listing and the office manager page, and its unreadable sitemap: a readable sitemap would give the first cadence reading.

The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile, and an unblocked Transparency Center lookup would settle the Paid Search test.
